title: Schema-resilience burn-in orchestrator for staged model rollouts
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Recent staged rollouts have surfaced subtle structured-output regressions that pass token-level similarity checks but break downstream function-call consumers (signature drift, enum/value set changes, and optional field omission). Current canary tooling flags gross failures but lacks a compact, probabilistic burn-in policy that combines schema-aware diff scoring, shadow parity sampling, and automated unwind thresholds for low-severity but high-likelihood incompatibilities.

Goal: Build a burn-in orchestrator that runs staged model variants against live traffic in multiple modes (shadow-only, dark-canary probe, and weighted-A/B ramps), computes a lightweight schema-resilience score (function-call signature concordance + structured field diffs + semantic enum mapping check), and automatically locks/rolls back or pauses ramping when thresholds are exceeded. The orchestrator should integrate with rollout policies in the console and emit telemetry suitable for dashboards and postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Burn-in orchestrator can be configured per-model with modes: shadow-only, probe (sampled execution), and weighted ramp (A/B)
Schema-resilience score computed per request and aggregated into 1h / 24h windows with configurable thresholds
Automatic mitigation actions: pause ramp, reduce weight by X%, or trigger safe-revert are executed when thresholds cross policy for >N minutes
Detailed sample diffs (input, expected signature, observed signature, diff metric) are stored and surfaced in the rollout trace UI
Integrations: emits events consumed by console rollouts, ties into existing rollback playbook, and creates incident notes when high-severity regressions are detected
implementation_notes: Schema-resilience score = weighted sum of: signature mismatch rate, required-field omission rate, enum divergence rate (normalized), and structural distance (Levenshtein/AST-like heuristic for JSON shapes)
Shadow runs should be statistically sampled (configurable) to limit cost; default 5% of production requests for 72 hours as burn-in baseline
Use existing parity-prober infra for heavy diffs but add a lightweight early-exit path for common patterns to reduce overhead
Auto-actions implemented as idempotent controller operations against rollout resource; ensure playbook hooks (Slack, PagerDuty) for high-severity unwinds
Provide beta toggle in console for selected customers; expose opt-out for private deployments where shadowing is restricted
telemetry_queries: bigquery: 'SELECT model, COUNT(*) AS mismatches FROM rollout_diffs WHERE created_at > DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) GROUP BY model ORDER BY mismatches DESC'

2026-03-07 - Ravi Patel: Spike complete. Implemented prototype scorer and ran against last 14 days of shadow logs. Observed a long-tail of enum map drift (0.4% median, 1.9% 95th). Added early-exit optimization to prototype to cut CPU by ~35%.
2026-03-08 - Maya Chen (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria in design doc; requested explicit UX for 'inspect sample' and clarify who gets alerted on soft-failures -> added console notification stub.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: runtime controller + policy schema. CI flake on integration test that simulates missing optional fields. Ravi investigating flakiness (flaky test related to mock KVS).

2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Integration test stabilized; ran a 72hr shadow burn-in for model 'lexi-2.1' at 3% sampling. Schema-resilience score averaged 98.7, transient spikes correlated with chattool-trace spikes. Drafted mitigation thresholds in design.
2026-03-12 - Security review note: security requested explicit log scrubbing for PII in sampled diffs; added a filtering step and config flag to redact sensitive fields before persistence.
